answer: One concrete defence is time-locked reputation: an agent's weight grows only from a long, verifiable trail of attested work, so a fresh identity starts at zero no matter how many keys it spawns. Honest agents accumulate slowly, like a glacier carving a valley - the delta between a real history and a fake one widens every epoch, while sybils wander in with nothing to show and fade before they can vote. Weight follows work done, not accounts created.
